description: Final allocation benchmark (repo code, mappo_v6 checkpoint, 200k steps, corrected semantics). 6 held-out maps x 4 episodes per policy = 24 episodes; 3 robots, 5 victims, 600-step cap unless noted. Values are mean +/- std.
provenance: training/evaluate.py runs of 2026-11 (Colab T4), repo commit with mappo_v6 contract (52-extras, sequential selection, invalid-action masking). Argmax = deterministic mode; sampled = deployment default (sample_actions:=true).
key_findings: Every three-robot configuration outperformed every single-robot configuration (lowest 3-robot coverage 76% argmax > highest single-robot 42%).
MAPPO in deployment mode (sampled) matches the greedy rule: coverage 86% vs 83%, victims 3.75 vs 3.92 (within one std); the rule finishes faster (196 vs 357 steps).
Simple commitment heuristics (sticky-unclaimed: keep region until exhausted, never poach a teammate's) set the bar: 89% coverage, 4.08 victims, 139 steps.
MAPPO argmax had not fully converged at 200k steps (76% coverage, 12/24 episodes hitting the step cap); policy entropy was still declining when training stopped.
